boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Arizona State University Campus Immersion
boards.description: Build an under-21-safe late-night ritual board. Every card needs a currently verifiable destination, a direct source supporting late availability, and a conservative explanation of why it matters near this campus. Do not invent student habits, signature orders, popularity, or current hours. Bars and 21+-only venues are prohibited.

cards.title: Gus's New York Pizza
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Pizza on Rural Road
cards.notes: Order a slice at this 24-hour staple located just east of campus. It is a reliable destination for students needing a meal during overnight study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour pizza shop on Rural Road serving the ASU community at all hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Gus's New York Pizza at 829 S Rural Rd is open 24 hours a day for pickup and delivery.
cards.source_title: Gus New York Pizza Tempe AZ - Pizza Delivery 24 hours a day
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for walk-ins, pickup, and delivery.

cards.title: Filiberto's Mexican Food
cards.subtitle: 24/7 Mexican Food on Apache Blvd
cards.notes: Visit this 24-hour Mexican spot for carne asada fries or burritos. It is located near the south edge of campus and stays open through the night.
cards.short_summary: A 24/7 Mexican restaurant on Apache Boulevard popular for late-night meals.
cards.evidence_claim: Filiberto's Mexican Food at 1270 E Apache Blvd offers 24/7 service for walk-in and drive-thru customers.
cards.source_title: Filibertos Mexican Food – Arizona's Favorite Mexican Food
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies
cards.subtitle: Warm Cookies Until 3 AM
cards.notes: Stop by for warm cookies or ice cream sandwiches until 3 AM on weekends. This bakery is a frequent late-night stop for students in Downtown Tempe.
cards.short_summary: A late-night bakery in Downtown Tempe serving warm cookies until 3 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies at 116 E University Dr is open until 1 AM Sunday-Wednesday and 3 AM Thursday-Saturday.
cards.source_title: Insomnia Cookies | Downtown Tempe
cards.access_notes: Open until 3 AM on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday nights.

cards.title: Dutch Bros Coffee
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Caffeine on Apache Blvd
cards.notes: Grab a Rebel energy drink or a coffee at this drive-thru stand open until 11 PM or midnight. It is a common stop for students on the south side of campus.
cards.short_summary: A popular drive-thru coffee stand on Apache Boulevard with late-night hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Dutch Bros Coffee at 1037 E Apache Blvd is open until 11 PM Sunday-Thursday and 12 AM Friday-Saturday.
cards.source_title: Tempe, AZ - Dutch Bros Coffee
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru open until midnight on weekends.

cards.title: Raising Cane's
cards.subtitle: Chicken Fingers Near Campus
cards.notes: Visit the University Drive location for chicken finger combos until 2 AM. The drive-thru is a frequent late-night destination for students.
cards.short_summary: A fast-food restaurant on University Drive open until 2 AM for late-night dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Raising Cane's at 960 E University Dr is open until 2 AM daily.
cards.source_title: Raising Cane's in Tempe, AZ, - 960 E. University Drive
cards.access_notes: Open until 2 AM every night.

cards.title: Cheba Hut
cards.subtitle: Toasted Subs Until Midnight
cards.notes: Order a toasted sub and 'munchies' at this themed sandwich shop until midnight. It is located just west of the main campus area.
cards.short_summary: A themed sandwich shop on University Drive serving toasted subs until midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Cheba Hut at 960 W University Dr is open until midnight every day of the week.
cards.source_title: Sandwiches & Sub Shop in Tempe 85281 - Cheba Hut
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight daily.

cards.title: Munchie Stop
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Mediterranean on Mill
cards.notes: Head to Mill Avenue for late-night Mediterranean food and wings. This spot operates specifically during late-night hours, often until 5 AM.
cards.short_summary: A late-night Mediterranean eatery on Mill Avenue operating until 5 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Munchie Stop at 1020 S Mill Ave is open from 9:30 PM to 5:00 AM daily.
cards.source_title: Info & Hours | Munchie Stop - Beyond Menu
cards.access_notes: Open late night only, from 9:30 PM to 5 AM.

cards.title: Memorial Union P.O.D. Market
cards.subtitle: On-Campus Convenience Until 10 PM
cards.notes: Grab snacks or a quick meal at the central campus P.O.D. Market. It serves as a primary late-evening resource for students in the Memorial Union.
cards.short_summary: A central campus convenience store in the Memorial Union open until 10 PM.
cards.evidence_claim: The P.O.D. Market in the Memorial Union is open until 10 PM Monday through Sunday during the academic semester.
cards.source_title: Tempe | Sun Devil Hospitality - Arizona State University
cards.access_notes: Open until 10 PM daily during the semester.

cards.title: Tooker House P.O.D. Market
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Snacks for Engineers
cards.notes: Visit the P.O.D. Market at Tooker House for late-night snacks and 'Tenders, Love, and Chicken.' It is a key resource for students on the north side of campus.
cards.short_summary: A convenience store and grill located in Tooker House serving students late into the night.
cards.evidence_claim: Tooker House P.O.D. Market is open until 2 AM for late-night dining and snacks.
cards.source_title: Tempe | Sun Devil Hospitality - Arizona State University
cards.access_notes: Open until 2 AM for late-night service.

cards.title: Snakes & Lattes
cards.subtitle: Board Games and Late-Night Snacks
cards.notes: Play board games while enjoying snacks and coffee at this 6th Street venue. It provides a social, alcohol-free alternative for late-night hangouts.
cards.short_summary: A board game cafe in Downtown Tempe offering late-night gaming and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Snakes & Lattes Tempe is open until 11 PM or later, hosting trivia and social gaming events for students.
cards.source_title: Board Game Bar & Restaurant in Tempe, AZ - Snakes & Lattes
cards.access_notes: Open until 11 PM or midnight depending on the day; under-21 friendly.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study nooks, quiet courtyards, and high-vantage points that ASU students use to escape the bustle of the Tempe campus.

cards.title: The Secret Garden
cards.subtitle: Between Dixie Gammage Hall and West Hall
cards.notes: Enter through the inconspicuous stairwells at Dixie Gammage Hall to find this sunken, grassy courtyard used for quiet reading and outdoor breaks.
cards.short_summary: A secluded, sunken courtyard hidden between historic campus buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Secret Garden is a beloved quiet spot hidden between Dixie Gammage Hall and West Hall, often used by students for solitude.
cards.source_title: Hidden gems at ASU
cards.access_notes: Open public outdoor space; most quiet during evening hours.

cards.title: Luhrs Arizona Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library, Level 1
cards.notes: Visit this first-floor room for a focused, silent environment surrounded by Arizona-themed collections and rotating cultural exhibits.
cards.short_summary: A silent reading room on the first floor of Hayden Library featuring Arizona collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Luhrs Arizona Reading Room on the first floor of Hayden Library offers a quiet space for focused studying and houses print collections pertaining to Arizona.
cards.source_title: First floor featured collections - ASU Library
cards.access_notes: Open during Hayden Library hours; typically 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. on weekdays.

cards.title: Life Sciences Tower Lookout
cards.subtitle: Life Sciences Center, 7th Floor
cards.notes: Take the elevator to the top floor of the E Wing to access a quiet landing with expansive views of 'A' Mountain and the Tempe skyline.
cards.short_summary: A high-vantage point on the top floor of the Life Sciences Tower offering views of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The seventh floor of the Life Sciences Center (E Wing) provides a lookout point with views of Hayden Lawn and downtown Phoenix.
cards.source_title: The best places on ASU's Tempe campus to relax and unwind
cards.access_notes: Accessible via elevator in the E Wing during building hours.

cards.title: Student Services Courtyard
cards.subtitle: 1151 S. Forest Ave
cards.notes: Find the tables tucked along the sides of this grassy courtyard for a silent outdoor study spot away from the main campus thoroughfares.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, grassy outdoor courtyard adjacent to the Student Services Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The courtyard next to the Student Services Building is an underappreciated silent outdoor spot with tables and chairs.
cards.source_title: 5 hidden study spots on ASU's Tempe campus
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor area; accessible 24/7 but best during daylight.

cards.title: ISTB4 Third Floor Nooks
cards.subtitle: Interdisciplinary Science and Technology IV
cards.notes: Explore the third floor for secluded seating areas that offer a quieter environment than the more popular library hubs.
cards.short_summary: Secluded study seating located on the third floor of the ISTB4 research building.
cards.evidence_claim: The third floor of ISTB4 often provides a quiet environment with lots of seating and a more secluded feel than popular study spots.
cards.source_title: Best Study Spots: ASU
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; typically 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. on weekdays.

cards.title: Noble Library Silent Zone
cards.subtitle: 601 E. Tyler Mall
cards.notes: Head to the second floor for designated quiet zones and individual study rooms that are ideal for intense, distraction-free work.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated silent study area on the second floor of the Noble Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Noble Library has designated quiet zones on the second floor and more than 75 study rooms for individual or group use.
cards.source_title: Study rooms in Noble Library - ASU Library
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; check the ASU Library website for current daily schedules.

cards.title: Student Pavilion Lounges
cards.subtitle: 400 E. Orange Street
cards.notes: Use the open lounge spaces on the second floor for group collaboration or casual study in a modern, net-zero energy building.
cards.short_summary: Modern lounge and study spaces on the second floor of the Student Pavilion.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Pavilion's second floor houses office space for student government and open areas suitable for student use.
cards.source_title: Student Pavilion - Educational Outreach and Student Services
cards.access_notes: General building hours are 7 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. Monday through Friday.

cards.title: Design Library Silent Room
cards.subtitle: Design North Building, Level 1
cards.notes: Utilize one of the largest silent study rooms on campus, featuring individual carrels and large tables for spreading out projects.
cards.short_summary: A large, dedicated silent study room within the Design and the Arts Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Design and the Arts Library boasts one of the largest silent study rooms with tables and individual study carrels.
cards.source_title: Looking for quiet study space? We got you covered - ASU Library
cards.access_notes: Open to ASU students and staff; visitors have limited hours.

cards.title: Music Library Quiet Nooks
cards.subtitle: Music Building, East Wing
cards.notes: Find near-silent study spots on the west side of the library, often less crowded than the main campus libraries.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study nooks located within the specialized Music Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Music Library provides near-silent study on its west side with study nooks and tables.
cards.source_title: Best Study Spots: ASU
cards.access_notes: Open during Music Library hours; typically 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays.

cards.title: Planetary Health Courtyard
cards.subtitle: University Dr & Rural Rd
cards.notes: Relax in the geode-inspired interior courtyard, designed with riparian features and cool blue-green walls to mimic a desert oasis.
cards.short_summary: A desert-inspired interior courtyard within the Walton Center for Planetary Health.
cards.evidence_claim: The Walton Center for Planetary Health features an interior courtyard modeled after a geode with a riparian area and light-filled spaces.
cards.source_title: The Rob and Melani Walton Center for Planetary Health at Arizona State University: Case Study
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during building hours; includes exhibit spaces.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Explore Arizona State University's Tempe campus with these social and cultural activities that require no admission fee or purchase. From world-class art galleries to serene desert gardens, these spots offer enriching experiences for students and the public alike.

cards.title: ASU Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Contemporary Art & Ceramics
cards.notes: Visit this contemporary museum for free exhibitions focusing on social justice and a renowned ceramics collection. It is open to the public Thursday through Sunday.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary art museum on the Tempe campus offering free admission to all visitors.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the ASU Art Museum is always free, and membership is not required to visit.
cards.source_title: ASU Art Museum Membership Subscription
cards.access_notes: Open Thursday-Sunday, 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. Admission is free for students and the general public.

cards.title: The Secret Garden
cards.subtitle: Secluded Campus Courtyard
cards.notes: Find this quiet courtyard tucked between Dixie Gammage Hall and West Hall. It features a lush lawn and fireplace, perfect for a peaceful study break or social gathering.
cards.short_summary: A hidden, landscaped courtyard in the heart of the Tempe campus known for its tranquil atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The Secret Garden is a secluded courtyard nestled in between buildings Dixie Gammage Hall and West Hall in the heart of the Tempe campus.
cards.source_title: Final Tempe Map - Colored (SDG) - ASU Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor space located in the interior of the Dixie Gammage Hall complex.

cards.title: Meteorite Gallery
cards.subtitle: Buseck Center for Meteorite Studies
cards.notes: Touch real meteorites and view one of the world's largest university collections. Located on the second floor of ISTB4, this gallery offers free self-guided tours.
cards.short_summary: A science gallery featuring rare lunar and Martian meteorites with free public access.
cards.evidence_claim: The display is open to the public for self-guided tours Monday through Friday, from 9 AM to 5 PM... Admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Visit the Buseck Center for Meteorite Studies - Arizona State University
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Closed on university holidays.

cards.title: James Turrell's Air Apparent
cards.subtitle: Public Art Installation
cards.notes: Experience this immersive light installation by artist James Turrell. It is most vibrant during sunrise and sunset when LED lights interact with the changing sky.
cards.short_summary: A permanent outdoor Skyspace installation that uses light and architecture to reframe the sky.
cards.evidence_claim: This work is open to the public '24/7'... Air Apparent is located near the intersection of Rural and Terrace roads.
cards.source_title: ASU unveils 'Air Apparent' – new public art space by James Turrell
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 to the public. Located northeast of the ISTB4 building.

cards.title: Walk the Iconic Palm Walk
cards.subtitle: Campus Pedestrian Mall
cards.notes: Stroll down the most photographed path on campus, lined with over 100 date palms. This 0.4-mile corridor connects the University Bridge to the fitness complex.
cards.short_summary: A scenic pedestrian thoroughfare lined with iconic palm trees, central to the ASU Tempe experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Palm Walk is the most photographed site on the Tempe campus... extending from the University Bridge on the north to the Sun Devil Fitness Complex on the south.
cards.source_title: Palm Walk | Virtual Tours - Arizona State University
cards.access_notes: Public pedestrian walkway accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Desert Arboretum Park
cards.subtitle: Botanical Refuge
cards.notes: Explore this 2.5-acre park featuring desert gardens and aquatic habitats. It serves as a botanical refuge for native plants tucked into the side of Tempe Butte.
cards.short_summary: A compact botanical park on the edge of campus showcasing southwestern desert flora.
cards.evidence_claim: Tucked into the side of Tempe Butte is the Desert Arboretum Park, a 2.5-acre botanical park... open and accessible to the public.
cards.source_title: Arboretum – Tempe campus - ASU Business and Finance
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during daylight hours. Located near Sun Devil Stadium.

cards.title: Gallery 100
cards.subtitle: Student Art Showcase
cards.notes: View rotating exhibitions of senior BFA student work, including ceramics, photography, and sculpture. The gallery is located in the Mirabella at ASU complex.
cards.short_summary: A university art gallery showcasing the thesis work of emerging student artists.
cards.evidence_claim: Gallery 100 is accessible to the local community as well as ASU's art students... Admission is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Gallery 100 - School of Art - Arizona State University
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday, 12 p.m. to 5 p.m. during the academic semester.

cards.title: Foucault Pendulum
cards.subtitle: Bateman Physical Sciences Center
cards.notes: Watch the Earth's rotation in real-time at one of the world's largest Foucault pendulums. It is located in the lobby of the Bateman Physical Sciences Center F-wing.
cards.short_summary: A large-scale scientific instrument on public display that demonstrates the rotation of the Earth.
cards.evidence_claim: The lobby contains a public display of rock types, and it also has one of the world's largest Foucault pendulums.
cards.source_title: Bateman Physical Sciences Center - Virtual Tours - Arizona State University
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building business hours, typically Monday-Friday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

cards.title: Create at the Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Creative Technology Lab
cards.notes: Use 3D printers, audio/video studios, and sewing machines for free. Located on the 3rd floor of Hayden Library, it is open to all students with a Sun Card.
cards.short_summary: A high-tech studio providing free access to creative equipment and workshops for the ASU community.
cards.evidence_claim: ASU Library's Makerspace is a high-tech studio... that all ASU students can use for free. We're talking equipment like 3D printers, a full video and audio studio.
cards.source_title: Free with tuition! - Hey Sunny - Arizona State University
cards.access_notes: Open weekdays 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Requires ASU ID (Sun Card) for equipment use.

cards.title: Mars Space Flight Facility
cards.subtitle: NASA Mission Operations
cards.notes: See a full-size Mars rover model in the lobby and learn about active NASA missions. Public tours are free and provide a look at how scientists study the Red Planet.
cards.short_summary: A research facility where students and the public can explore Mars exploration history and current missions.
cards.evidence_claim: Tours of MSFF are free and open to the public... On display at the facility we host a full-size Mars rover (Opportunity) model.
cards.source_title: Mars Space Flight Facility Tours at ASU - Mars Education
cards.access_notes: Lobby is open to the public weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Group tours require advance request.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Discover a range of study environments across the Tempe campus, from silent library carrels to collaborative student lounges and specialized academic halls.

cards.title: Silent Study with Brody Chairs
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library
cards.notes: Head to the top floor for a traditional library feel. Use the Brody chairs for integrated power, lighting, and high-walled privacy during long writing sessions.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, traditional library floor featuring specialized privacy seating and individual carrels.
cards.evidence_claim: Level 4 of Hayden Library offers Brody chairs equipped with light and power, individual study carrels, and comfortable seating with power outlets.
cards.source_title: Looking for quiet study space? We got you covered - ASU Library
cards.access_notes: Open to current ASU students; check library hours for daily access.

cards.title: First-Come Solo Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Noble Library
cards.notes: Find one of 55 individual rooms on the second and third floors. These are available on a first-come, first-served basis and provide a desk, chair, and outlet.
cards.short_summary: Dozens of private, single-person study rooms available without prior reservation.
cards.evidence_claim: Noble Library has 55 individual study rooms on the second and third floors available on a first-come, first-served basis.
cards.source_title: Study rooms in Noble Library - ASU Library
cards.access_notes: No keys or reservations required; one person maximum per room.

cards.entity_name: Design and the Arts Library Silent Room
cards.title: The Large Silent Study Room
cards.subtitle: Design North Building
cards.notes: Utilize one of the largest silent study rooms on campus. It features long tables and individual carrels specifically designed for focused, distraction-free work.
cards.short_summary: A spacious, dedicated silent study environment located within the Design North building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Design and the Arts Library boasts one of the largest silent study rooms with tables, comfortable chairs, and individual study carrels.
cards.source_title: Looking for quiet study space? We got you covered - ASU Library
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of Design North; open during standard library hours.

cards.title: Near-Silent Nooks and Tables
cards.subtitle: Music Building West
cards.notes: Visit the west side of the third floor for a near-silent environment. This area is often less crowded and offers study carrels and comfortable seating.
cards.short_summary: A quiet study area on the third floor of the Music Building, ideal for escaping central campus crowds.
cards.evidence_claim: The Music Library provides near-silent study on the west side of the library with study carrels, tables, and comfortable seating.
cards.source_title: Looking for quiet study space? We got you covered - ASU Library
cards.access_notes: Located on the third floor of Music Building West; check specific library hours.

cards.title: Calm Collaborative Lounges
cards.subtitle: Student Pavilion
cards.notes: Head to the second floor for a calmer environment than the first-floor hub. It offers open seating and a patio for group work or individual focus.
cards.short_summary: A sustainable, student-centric building offering quiet study areas on its upper floors.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Pavilion's second floor and above provide a calm environment perfect for focused individual study.
cards.source_title: Best Study Spots: ASU - Untapped Learning
cards.access_notes: General building hours are 7 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. on weekdays.

cards.title: High-Tech Collaboration Spaces
cards.subtitle: W.P. Carey School of Business
cards.notes: Reserve one of 59 team rooms equipped with large screen displays and whiteboards. These spaces are designed for group projects and professional collaboration.
cards.short_summary: Modern, reservable rooms for groups of up to six people within the business school complex.
cards.evidence_claim: McCord Hall features 59 six-person team rooms equipped with large screen displays and white boards to support group learning.
cards.source_title: W.P Carey School of Business McCord Hall - KPF
cards.access_notes: Primarily for business students; check reservation portal for availability.

cards.title: Renovated Silent Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: Durham Hall
cards.notes: Explore the fourth floor of this recently renovated building for a quiet study area. It offers a modern environment away from the busier central campus hubs.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, modernized study space located on the upper floor of Durham Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Durham Hall's fourth floor is noted as a silent study area following its comprehensive interior renovation.
cards.source_title: Durham Hall - ASU Business and Finance
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; accessible via the new gurney-sized elevator.

cards.title: Secluded Seating and Outlets
cards.subtitle: Interdisciplinary Science and Technology Building 4
cards.notes: Find a spot on the third floor for a more secluded feel. This area provides plenty of seating and outlets, often remaining quieter than the main libraries.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, less-trafficked study area with ample seating in a modern research building.
cards.evidence_claim: The third floor of ISTB4 provides a quiet environment with lots of seating and a more secluded feel than popular study spots.
cards.source_title: Best Study Spots: ASU - Untapped Learning
cards.access_notes: Building and elevators may lock after 5 p.m.; best for daytime study.

cards.title: Serene Study with a View
cards.subtitle: Memorial Union
cards.notes: Gather in this main-level lounge for views of Cady Mall. It features high-backed chairs and a fireplace, providing a serene space for rest and study.
cards.short_summary: A popular, comfortable lounge in the student union known for its fireplace and campus views.
cards.evidence_claim: Scoular Lounge in the Memorial Union provides a serene space for rest, relaxation, and collaboration with views of Cady Mall.
cards.source_title: Memorial Union Lounges - ASU Educational Outreach and Student Services
cards.access_notes: Open during Memorial Union building hours; check for seasonal fireplace use.

cards.title: Quiet Reading and Collections
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library
cards.notes: Visit the first floor for a quiet reading atmosphere. This room houses featured collections and exhibits, offering a peaceful alternative to the busier floors.
cards.short_summary: A quiet reading room on the first floor of Hayden Library focused on Arizona collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Luhrs Reading Room on the ground floor of Hayden Library provides an atmosphere of quiet and is open to all.
cards.source_title: Looking for quiet study space? We got you covered - ASU Library
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor; open to all visitors during library hours.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors immediately surrounding the ASU Tempe campus, from the high-energy retail of Mill Avenue to the student-centric hubs along Apache Boulevard.

cards.title: The Historic Retail Hub
cards.subtitle: Mill Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this historic stretch for a mix of local boutiques, national retailers, and diverse dining options located just steps from the campus's western edge.
cards.short_summary: A vibrant commercial corridor featuring historic architecture and a high density of student-oriented shops and restaurants.
cards.evidence_claim: Mill Avenue is recognized as the central hub for Tempe shopping, dining, and recreation, built around Arizona State University.
cards.source_title: Retail Space Available | Invest - Downtown Tempe
cards.access_notes: Public street with 24/7 pedestrian access; business hours vary by establishment.

cards.title: The Modern Campus Connector
cards.subtitle: College Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Visit this multi-modal streetscape north of University Drive to find the Sun Devil Marketplace and flexible public plaza spaces for community events.
cards.short_summary: A transformed urban block featuring the Sun Devil Marketplace and sustainable academic facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: College Avenue Commons is a mixed-use facility on College Avenue one block north of University Drive, housing the Sun Devil Marketplace.
cards.source_title: Paul C. Helmick Center - ASU Business and Finance
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; marketplace typically open daily during standard retail hours.

cards.title: The Residential Gateway
cards.subtitle: Apache Boulevard Corridor
cards.notes: Explore this corridor on the south side of campus, home to major student housing complexes and convenient on-site retail like Shibam Coffee.
cards.short_summary: A high-density residential and retail corridor serving students on the southern edge of the Tempe campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The District on Apache is located within walking distance of the ASU campus and features onsite retail like Shibam Coffee.
cards.source_title: The District on Apache: Neighborhood
cards.access_notes: Public sidewalks and retail spaces; residential areas require keycard access.

cards.title: The Northern Perimeter
cards.subtitle: University Drive Corridor
cards.notes: Walk along this major thoroughfare to access off-campus apartments and quick-service dining options just north of the main academic buildings.
cards.short_summary: A primary east-west corridor bordering the northern edge of campus with numerous student housing options.
cards.evidence_claim: Paseo on University offers student lifestyle housing near ASU, located along the University Drive corridor.
cards.source_title: Paseo on University - ASU Off-Campus Student Housing
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; retail and housing access varies.

cards.title: The Modern Living Block
cards.subtitle: Terrace Road Corridor
cards.notes: Check out this emerging block featuring new high-rise student communities like VERVE Tempe and Vertex Apartments near the light rail.
cards.short_summary: A concentrated block of modern student housing developments located southeast of the main campus.
cards.evidence_claim: VERVE Tempe is a 15-story student housing community located at 1047 S Terrace Rd, steps from ASU.
cards.source_title: VERVE Tempe Student Living Community | Subtext
cards.access_notes: Public street access; residential amenities for residents only.

cards.title: The West Campus Edge
cards.subtitle: Forest Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Stop by this street for local favorites like Harry's Coffee Shop, providing a quieter alternative to the main Mill Avenue bustle.
cards.short_summary: A street bordering the western campus edge known for its local dining and student-friendly atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: Harry's Coffee Shop is located at 715 S Forest Ave, serving as a classic diner for the ASU community.
cards.source_title: Union Tempe | Downtown Tempe
cards.access_notes: Public street; business hours vary.

cards.title: The Eastern Transit Link
cards.subtitle: Rural Road Corridor
cards.notes: Use this major north-south corridor to access the University Drive/Rural Road light rail station and eastern campus housing like Sonora Center.
cards.short_summary: A primary transportation artery on the eastern edge of campus connecting students to the light rail and housing.
cards.evidence_claim: Sonora Center is located at 1480 S. Rural Rd, providing housing for first-year students on the south side of campus.
cards.source_title: Sonora Center - ASU Housing
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; light rail station accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Historic Neighborhood
cards.subtitle: Ash Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk through this quiet residential street to see historic bungalows and mature trees in one of Tempe's most walkable off-campus neighborhoods.
cards.short_summary: A historic residential district west of Mill Avenue offering a quieter, pedestrian-friendly environment.
cards.evidence_claim: The Residences on Ash are situated on the quiet residential Ash Avenue within walking distance to downtown Tempe and ASU.
cards.source_title: The Residences on Ash - 1209 S Ash Ave Tempe AZ
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; please respect resident privacy.

cards.title: The Stadium Gateway
cards.subtitle: 5th Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the retail spaces near the Veterans Way light rail station, serving as a primary path for fans heading to Mountain America Stadium.
cards.short_summary: A retail-heavy block near the light rail station and athletic facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: 200 East Fifth Street offers retail space near the Veterans Way light rail station and ASU stadium.
cards.source_title: 200 East Fifth Street | Downtown Tempe
cards.access_notes: Public street; retail hours vary.

cards.title: The Waterfront District
cards.subtitle: Rio Salado Parkway Corridor
cards.notes: Walk north to the lakefront for scenic paths and major events at Tempe Beach Park, located just north of the campus core.
cards.short_summary: A scenic waterfront corridor offering recreational paths and event spaces north of the university.
cards.evidence_claim: Tempe Town Lake is a man-made oasis with paths for jogging and free events, located near the ASU campus.
cards.source_title: Tempe Town Lake | City of Tempe, AZ
cards.access_notes: Park paths open daily from 5:00 AM to 12:00 AM.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From painting the iconic mountain to the lighting of lanterns, Arizona State University's traditions are deeply rooted in its desert history and Sun Devil spirit.

cards.title: Echo from the Buttes
cards.subtitle: Whitewashing the 'A' Mountain
cards.notes: Hike up Hayden Butte during Welcome Week to paint the 60-foot concrete 'A' white, symbolizing a fresh start for the incoming class.
cards.short_summary: A Welcome Week tradition where freshmen hike Hayden Butte to paint the iconic 'A' white.
cards.evidence_claim: Echo from the Buttes is a cherished, 80-plus-year tradition where incoming first-year students hike up 'A' Mountain to paint the letter white each August.
cards.source_title: Echo from the Buttes: Honoring tradition, culture and heritage
cards.access_notes: Open to all incoming students during Fall Welcome Week; requires a hike up the butte.

cards.title: Lantern Walk
cards.subtitle: A Century-Old Homecoming Ritual
cards.notes: Carry a lantern to the top of 'A' Mountain on the Friday night before the Homecoming game to hear speakers and see the royalty coronation.
cards.short_summary: One of ASU's oldest traditions, where students and alumni carry lanterns up 'A' Mountain before Homecoming.
cards.evidence_claim: Lantern Walk was first celebrated in 1917 and involves students and alumni climbing to the top of 'A' Mountain carrying lanterns on the Friday night before the Homecoming game.
cards.source_title: Traditions - ASU Homecoming
cards.access_notes: Held annually on the Friday night of Homecoming week.

cards.title: Ringing the Victory Bell
cards.subtitle: Commemorating Sun Devil Triumphs
cards.notes: Watch the Victory Bell Honor Guard ring the portable 150-pound bell after every home win to celebrate the team's success.
cards.short_summary: A restored 1930s tradition where a bell is rung to celebrate athletic victories.
cards.evidence_claim: The Victory Bell tradition dates back to the 1930s and was restored in 2012 with a new 150-pound bell that is rung after every Sun Devil triumph.
cards.source_title: Sun Devil Athletics brings back Victory Bell in return to tradition
cards.access_notes: The bell is present at home football games and other major athletic events.

cards.title: Touching the Tillman Statue
cards.subtitle: Honoring a Sun Devil Legend
cards.notes: Observe the football team touch the 7.5-foot bronze statue of Pat Tillman as they charge through the tunnel onto Frank Kush Field.
cards.short_summary: A pre-game ritual where players touch the Pat Tillman statue for inspiration.
cards.evidence_claim: Unveiled in 2017, the Pat Tillman statue stands in front of the Tillman Tunnel, and players touch it as they charge onto the field to honor his legacy.
cards.source_title: Enshrining a legend - ASU News
cards.access_notes: Located at the north end of Mountain America Stadium; visible during games.

cards.title: Camp Tontozona
cards.subtitle: Preseason Training in the Pines
cards.notes: Follow the team to the Mogollon Rim for grueling preseason practices, a tradition started by Coach Frank Kush in 1960.
cards.short_summary: The annual preseason football training camp held in the mountains near Payson, Arizona.
cards.evidence_claim: Camp Tontozona, or 'Camp T,' began in 1960 under Coach Frank Kush and continues as an annual August preseason training tradition for the football team.
cards.source_title: Bonding, bunk beds and ... a dead bat? An oral history of Camp Tontozona
cards.access_notes: Located 17.9 miles outside of Payson; fans often travel to watch the final practice.

cards.title: Forks Up
cards.subtitle: The Universal Sun Devil Greeting
cards.notes: Extend your index, middle, and pinky fingers to form the pitchfork sign, the standard gesture of school spirit and greeting.
cards.short_summary: The iconic hand gesture representing Sparky's pitchfork and Sun Devil pride.
cards.evidence_claim: 'Forks Up' is the hand sign inspired by Sparky's pitchfork and is an essential part of ASU traditions and game day culture.
cards.source_title: Sun Devil Traditions | ASU Sun Devil Athletics
cards.access_notes: Used campus-wide and at all athletic events.

cards.title: Sparky's Push-ups
cards.subtitle: Scoring with the Mascot
cards.notes: Count along as Sparky the Sun Devil performs one push-up for every point on the scoreboard after each ASU touchdown.
cards.short_summary: A game day tradition where the mascot performs push-ups corresponding to the team's score.
cards.evidence_claim: When the Sun Devils score a touchdown, Sparky does one pushup for every point on the scoreboard while the crowd counts.
cards.source_title: Sun Devil Traditions | ASU Sun Devil Athletics
cards.access_notes: Occurs during home football games at Mountain America Stadium.

cards.title: Stomp the Bus
cards.subtitle: A Thunderstruck Entrance
cards.notes: Watch the video board as Sparky 'crushes' the opposing team's bus to the tune of AC/DC's 'Thunderstruck' before the team enters.
cards.short_summary: A pre-game video tradition where Sparky stomps on the opponent's bus.
cards.evidence_claim: Sparky leaves the opposing team 'thunderstruck' when he crushes their bus on the video board to welcome Sun Devil Football onto the field.
cards.source_title: Sun Devil Traditions | ASU Sun Devil Athletics
cards.access_notes: Played on the stadium big screen just before the team takes the field.

cards.title: Guarding the 'A'
cards.subtitle: Rivalry Week Vigilance
cards.notes: Join the Student Alumni Association in camping out on Hayden Butte to protect the 'A' from being painted by rival U of A students.
cards.short_summary: A rivalry week tradition where students protect the 'A' from vandals.
cards.evidence_claim: Every year during the rivalry football game week, the Student Alumni Association guards the 'A' from being painted by University of Arizona students.
cards.source_title: Traditions - ASU Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the week leading up to the Territorial Cup game.

cards.title: Sun Devil Walk
cards.subtitle: Greeting the Team
cards.notes: Line the path on College Avenue two hours before kickoff to cheer on the players, Sparky, and the band as they head to the stadium.
cards.short_summary: The pre-game procession of the football team and marching band through campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sun Devil Walk welcomes the football team to the stadium before the game with Sparky, the Spirit Squad, and the Sun Devil Marching Band.
cards.source_title: Sun Devil Traditions | ASU Sun Devil Athletics
cards.access_notes: Takes place on College Avenue approximately two and a half hours before home games.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Arizona State University Campus Immersion, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Check In at the Student Hub
cards.subtitle: The Living Room of Campus
cards.notes: Visit the MU to find the information desk, grab a meal at the food court, or relax in the lounges. It serves as the central meeting point for new students.
cards.short_summary: The Memorial Union is the central student hub at ASU Tempe, offering dining, meeting spaces, and student services.
cards.evidence_claim: The Memorial Union, known as the MU, is considered the living room of the campus and features dozens of dining options, lounges, and study spaces.
cards.source_title: The Memorial Union | Educational Outreach and Student Services
cards.access_notes: Open daily with extended hours during the academic year; check specific dining venue hours on the ASU website.

cards.title: Walk the Iconic Campus Path
cards.subtitle: A Century-Old Tradition
cards.notes: Stroll down this 0.4-mile pedestrian mall lined with over 100 date palms. It is the most photographed landmark on the Tempe campus.
cards.short_summary: Palm Walk is a famous pedestrian corridor at ASU Tempe, lined with iconic date palms and connecting major campus landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: Palm Walk is a pedestrian mall on the Tempe campus lined with 110 date palms, running nearly 0.4 miles from University Bridge to the Sun Devil Fitness Complex.
cards.source_title: Palm Walk rehabilitation - ASU Business and Finance
cards.access_notes: Public pedestrian path accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Tour the Reinvented Library
cards.subtitle: Academic Heart of Tempe
cards.notes: Explore five floors of study suites, innovation labs, and community book collections. Join a student-led walking tour to learn about research resources.
cards.short_summary: Hayden Library is the main library at ASU Tempe, recently renovated to include modern study spaces and interdisciplinary labs.
cards.evidence_claim: Hayden Library offers ample student space, collaborative study rooms, and interdisciplinary learning labs across a revamped five-story tower.
cards.source_title: Hayden Library - ASU Library
cards.access_notes: Open daily; ASU ID required for late-night access. Check the library website for current hours.

cards.title: Get Active at the SDFC
cards.subtitle: Wellness and Recreation
cards.notes: Use your student ID to access weight rooms, cardio equipment, and the pool. It's a great place to meet people through intramural sports or group classes.
cards.short_summary: The Sun Devil Fitness Complex (SDFC) provides comprehensive fitness and wellness facilities for ASU students.
cards.evidence_claim: The SDFC is a state-of-the-art fitness facility free for currently enrolled ASU students, featuring cardio equipment, pools, and group wellness classes.
cards.source_title: Sun Devil Fitness - Arizona State University
cards.access_notes: Access is free for enrolled students with a valid Sun Devil ID card.

cards.title: Attend Sun Devil Welcome
cards.subtitle: The Ultimate Spirit Event
cards.notes: Join thousands of first-year students for a high-energy introduction to ASU traditions, featuring the marching band and Sparky the Sun Devil.
cards.short_summary: Mountain America Stadium hosts the annual Sun Devil Welcome, a signature event for all incoming first-year students.
cards.evidence_claim: Sun Devil Welcome is a high-energy event for all ASU first-year students held inside Mountain America Stadium to celebrate spirit and tradition.
cards.source_title: ASU Welcome Signature Events
cards.access_notes: Event typically held in the evening during Welcome Week; check the ASU Welcome calendar for specific dates.

cards.title: Hike and Paint 'A' Mountain
cards.subtitle: A Rite of Passage
cards.notes: Hike up Hayden Butte to help paint the iconic 'A' white, signaling the start of the new school year. It's one of ASU's oldest traditions.
cards.short_summary: Whitewashing the 'A' is a long-standing tradition where new students hike 'A' Mountain to paint the letter white at the start of the year.
cards.evidence_claim: Whitewashing the 'A' on Hayden Butte is a wrap-up event of Welcome Week where every freshman is invited to paint the 'A' white.
cards.source_title: ASU Welcome Traditions
cards.access_notes: The hike is steep; students are encouraged to wear comfortable shoes and bring water.

cards.title: Explore Contemporary Art
cards.subtitle: Free Cultural Experience
cards.notes: Visit the museum to see rotating exhibitions of contemporary art. It's a quiet, air-conditioned space perfect for a weekend afternoon.
cards.short_summary: The ASU Art Museum is a leading contemporary art venue located on the Tempe campus, offering free admission to all visitors.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the ASU Art Museum and participation in nearly all of its events and programs is free.
cards.source_title: Visit the ASU Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday through Sunday, 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

cards.title: Discover Frank Lloyd Wright Architecture
cards.subtitle: Historic Performing Arts Center
cards.notes: Check out this iconic circular building designed by Frank Lloyd Wright. Look for $10 student tickets for select 'Beyond' series performances.
cards.short_summary: ASU Gammage is a historic theater on the Tempe campus known for its unique architecture and world-class performances.
cards.evidence_claim: $10 student tickets are available for all Beyond performances at ASU Gammage, subject to availability.
cards.source_title: Students | ASU Gammage
cards.access_notes: Box office hours vary; check the website for performance schedules and ticket availability.

cards.title: Find Your Student Club
cards.subtitle: Involvement Fair
cards.notes: Explore hundreds of student organizations at this massive involvement fair. It's the best way to find communities that share your interests.
cards.short_summary: Passport to ASU is a major involvement fair held during Welcome Week where students can explore and join various campus clubs.
cards.evidence_claim: Passport to ASU is the easiest way to explore all the ways to get involved, with clubs gathering around the Memorial Union and Student Pavilion.
cards.source_title: ASU Welcome Involvement Fairs
cards.access_notes: Typically held on a Friday or Saturday during the first weekend; check the official ASU Welcome schedule.

cards.title: Catch a Game or Event
cards.subtitle: Home of Sun Devil Athletics
cards.notes: Visit the arena for basketball games or university-wide events. It's a central venue for student life and athletic pride.
cards.short_summary: Desert Financial Arena is a multi-purpose indoor arena on the Tempe campus, hosting ASU basketball, volleyball, and major events.
cards.evidence_claim: Desert Financial Arena is the home of Sun Devil Men's and Women's Basketball and hosts various student events throughout the year.
cards.source_title: Desert Financial Arena - Sun Devil Athletics
cards.access_notes: Student tickets are often available through the Sun Devil Rewards app or athletics website.
